catalog_upserts.audit_note: Verified 2026-10-10 from Crossref and Europe PMC (Nat Biotechnol online 2025-05-23, CC BY; ChemRxiv v1 posted 2023-12-01 under an earlier title), the repository (MIT LICENSE; README links paper, weights, data and web app), Zenodo 10997887 (CC BY 4.0; embedding_model.ckpt, ssl_model.ckpt) and the Hugging Face API (ungated, card MIT; the same two checkpoints at identical byte sizes plus a MassSpecGym embedding checkpoint and a TorchScript export). The code downloads weights from the Hugging Face repo. The two weight hosts carry different licence labels. The Zenodo weights record has no Zenodo DOI and lists the ChemRxiv DOI as its PID. Upstream MassIVE terms for GeMS were not reviewed. No weights were downloaded or run.

catalog_upserts.name: CTransPath
catalog_upserts.description: Self-supervised histopathology tile encoder that couples a convolutional stem with a Swin Transformer (Swin-T) backbone. It was pretrained with semantically-relevant contrastive learning (SRCL) on about 15 million unlabelled TCGA and PAIP patches, and the authors recommend it as a frozen histopathology feature extractor.
catalog_upserts.status: Open code and public ungated weights (author Google Drive link). LICENSE.md is GPL-3.0, but the README states availability for non-commercial academic purposes only, and these terms conflict. There is no separate weight licence. Non-commercial terms apply to at least one artifact or access route.
catalog_upserts.io: H&E histology tile (224 px; README suggests about 1.0 mpp first) -> tile-level embedding
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Frozen tile features for patch classification and retrieval, and weakly supervised whole-slide classification (multiple-instance learning). Fine-tuning for mitosis detection and gland segmentation.
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Older catalog gap, verified on 2026-10-10 from Crossref, Europe PMC (abstract, PMID 35952419), the GitHub licence API, the README and the Drive file page; no weights were downloaded. LICENSE.md is unmodified GPL-3.0, but the README License section restricts use to non-commercial academic purposes, so noncommercial is set to true and the GPL/NC conflict is left unresolved. The weights are on a personal Drive with no weight licence and no checksum, and they need a modified timm 0.5.4 build, also on Drive. The same repo hosts separate TransPath (MICCAI 2021) and MoCo v3 checkpoints; these are not part of this record, and TransPath is not an alias. Hugging Face copies are third-party re-uploads.

catalog_upserts.name: GRASP
catalog_upserts.description: Molecular graph Transformer (93.5M parameters) pretrained by replaced-token detection on 1.54B ZINC20 molecule presentations and then adapted with sparse labels from 642 ChEMBL assays; the released 50,000-step Step 2 encoder provides 768-d molecular embeddings for downstream property models.
catalog_upserts.status: Public ungated weights (Hugging Face) and code (GitHub, no tagged release) under CC BY-NC 4.0 per LICENSE file, NOTICE and model card; MolE-derived code inherits CC BY-NC 4.0; bundled DeBERTa code MIT. README licence line changed to MIT on 2026-10-05 without changing LICENSE or NOTICE (conflict; non-commercial reading applied). Training data not redistributed; no hosted API.
catalog_upserts.io: SMILES (2D molecular graph) -> 768-d molecular embedding (final-layer CLS); embedding + labelled data -> fine-tuned property predictor (full, LoRA or frozen encoder)
catalog_upserts.use_cases: ADMET property prediction by fine-tuning (full, LoRA or frozen encoder), molecular embeddings for downstream property models, molecular representation learning
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Preprint only (bioRxiv, v2 posted 2026-10-06); README and model card cite an arXiv identifier as pending. LICENSE, NOTICE, vendored MolE licence and model card apply CC BY-NC 4.0; the README has said MIT since a 2026-10-05 commit, unresolved, so the non-commercial reading is used. Reuses MolE code but pretrains its own encoder; not a MolE re-release. Downstream evaluation covers ADMET endpoints only. Weights listed, not downloaded or executed.

catalog_upserts.name: LDDM (Large Drug Discovery Model)
catalog_upserts.description: Pocket-conditioned 3D generative model covering constrained and unconstrained docking, fragment linking and growing, and de novo ligand design in one model, with a programmable sampler for synthesizable designs.
catalog_upserts.io: Protein pocket structure (+ optional ligand fragments or constraints) -> 3D ligand poses or generated ligands
catalog_upserts.status: Open MIT code; Zenodo weights: paper checkpoint CC BY-NC 4.0 (BindingNet data), BindingNet-free checkpoint MIT; no hosted API; Enamine REAL design needs a separate Enamine licence
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Structure-based drug design, docking, fragment linking and growing, synthesizable analogue design
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Adversarial review 2026-10-10. Preprint only (bioRxiv published=NA); re-check for a journal version. Terms are checkpoint-specific: lddm.ckpt is CC BY-NC 4.0 because of BindingNet training data, lddm_CDBB.ckpt and the other Zenodo files are MIT, and the Zenodo record-level licence field reads MIT, so the per-checkpoint wording must be preserved. The preprint links only the GitHub repository; the Zenodo weights record is endorsed through the official README, not the paper. Enamine REAL synthesizable design requires a licence from Enamine; the shipped 44,944-block space is SynSpace/Mcule-derived. Weights verified from Zenodo metadata and file listing only, never downloaded or executed.

catalog_upserts.name: Zatom-1
catalog_upserts.description: Transformer (80M-300M parameters) trained with a multimodal flow-matching objective over discrete atom types and continuous 3D geometries, jointly pretrained on QM9 small molecules and MP20 crystals, with further GEOM-Drugs, QMOF and OMol25 pretraining checkpoints; the generative pretraining initialises downstream property, energy and force prediction.
catalog_upserts.status: LBNL modified-BSD code licence; public ungated weights on Hugging Face (card: MIT) and Zenodo (record: CC BY 4.0); no hosted API
catalog_upserts.io: Sampling from noise -> 3D molecules or crystals (atom types, coordinates, lattice); 3D molecular or crystal structure -> property, energy and force predictions via finetuned heads
catalog_upserts.use_cases: 3D small-molecule and crystal generation, molecular and materials property prediction, energy/force prediction, transfer learning
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Workshop paper (ICLR 2026 FM4Science) on arXiv. Licence labels differ across distributions but all are permissive: LBNL modified-BSD for code (the paper says 'permissive BSD'), an MIT tag in the HF card YAML (no LICENSE file in the HF repo), and CC BY 4.0 on the Zenodo record. The README downloads checkpoints from Zenodo; HF is an author-org mirror (org members are paper authors). Chemistry/materials model whose link to biology runs through small and drug-like molecules and an OMol25 checkpoint. Successor Zatom-2 (October 2026) is held for missing artifacts. Weights not executed.

catalog_upserts.name: AIMNet2
catalog_upserts.description: Atoms-in-molecules neural network potential for neutral and charged organic and element-organic molecules (up to 14 elements) combining learned short-range and physics-based long-range terms; family members cover reactive pathways (AIMNet2-rxn), open-shell species and palladium chemistry.
catalog_upserts.status: Open code + ungated weights (MIT) on GitHub and Hugging Face; AIMNet2 training data (MIT) on CMU KiltHub; AIMNet2-rxn archived on Zenodo (MIT); public web demo
catalog_upserts.io: 3D molecular structure with total charge (and spin multiplicity for the open-shell model) -> energies, forces, atomic charges, Hessians; stress for periodic systems
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Molecular dynamics, conformer search and torsion scans, reaction-path and transition-state search, drug-like and element-organic chemistry
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Family record; members differ in element and charge coverage (AIMNet2-rxn: closed-shell, net-neutral C, H, N, O). All five Isayev-lab HF repos (wb97m-d3, 2025, nse, pd, rxn) are ungated MIT; the AIMNet2 training datasets on CMU KiltHub are MIT; the AIMNet2-rxn reaction training set was not found among released files. The Science Advances article is CC BY-NC 4.0 and the Chem Sci article CC BY 3.0. These are article licences only, not code, weight or data terms. Publisher pages blocked automated fetch (403); metadata and full texts were read via Crossref and Europe PMC. Year follows the 2023 ChemRxiv preprint listed by Crossref. Not executed.

catalog_upserts.name: DPA4 / DPA4C (DeePMD-kit)
catalog_upserts.description: Universal equivariant machine-learned interatomic potentials implemented in DeePMD-kit: DPA4 (SeZM architecture) targets accuracy, and DPA4C is a compact, compressible variant for high-throughput, large-scale MD. Checkpoints trained on OMol25 (biomolecules, metal complexes, electrolytes) are intended for molecular systems; DPA4C-OMol has much higher molecular errors than DPA4-OMol. Materials checkpoints (OMat24) are released separately.
catalog_upserts.status: Open code (LGPL-3.0, DeePMD-kit 3.2.0+); public ungated checkpoints on Hugging Face under CC BY-NC 4.0 (declared in model-card metadata); training data are third-party public datasets
catalog_upserts.io: Atomic structure with total charge and spin multiplicity -> energies and forces
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Energy/force prediction and MD for molecules within OMol25 chemical space and for materials; large-scale MD (DPA4C); fine-tuning to system-specific potentials
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Materials-first family (DPA4 headline benchmark: Matbench Discovery); only the OMol25-trained checkpoints target molecules. On the OMol25 OOD composition split, DPA4C energy MAEs are 16.77-40.97 kcal/mol versus 0.92-8.02 for DPA4. Released OMol checkpoints are Air/Mini/Nano/Neo/Plus; DPA4-Pro is not released. MatPES-trained variants are benchmarked but not on the hub. Neither paper's availability statement mentions weights; the HF org is referenced by DeePMD-kit's pretrained registry, though the OMol repos are not listed there. Weight licence is CC BY-NC 4.0 in card metadata only, with no licence file; code is LGPL-3.0. Older DPA-2/DPA-3 checkpoints (CC BY 4.0) not assessed. Preprints only; weights not executed.

catalog_upserts.name: KERMT (Contrastive KERMT)
catalog_upserts.description: Graph-transformer molecular encoder for small-molecule property prediction. KERMT (Merck and NVIDIA, 2025) is an accelerated GROVER reimplementation for multitask fine-tuning that used the published GROVER weights. The released v2.0 checkpoint (Contrastive KERMT, NVIDIA, 2026) is pretrained on about 11M molecules. It keeps GROVER-style atom/bond/functional-group self-supervision and adds SMILES reconstruction and a contrastive (cMIM) objective, as a starting point for multi-task ADMET fine-tuning.
catalog_upserts.status: Apache-2.0 code (GitHub). Public, ungated v2.0 weights and vocab files on Hugging Face under the NVIDIA Open Model License: commercially usable; redistribution requires an attribution notice; rights terminate on guardrail circumvention or IP litigation. KERMT v1 benchmark splits on Figshare are labelled GPL.
catalog_upserts.io: SMILES (featurized into a 2D atom-bond graph) -> molecular embeddings; multi-task ADMET endpoint predictions after fine-tuning
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Multi-task ADMET/ADME fine-tuning, molecular feature extraction, representation-learning baseline for drug discovery; on-target potency fine-tuning reported only for KERMT v1
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Lineage: KERMT is an enhanced reimplementation of GROVER (existing bfm-grover). KERMT v1 (2025) shipped code only and fine-tuned the published GROVER base weights. The separate record rests on the independently pretrained v2.0 Contrastive KERMT checkpoint (NVIDIA, June 2026). The v2.0 pretraining corpus includes unlabeled molecules from its evaluation benchmarks (Biogen, ExpansionRX, ChEMBL-MT); the preprint reports these gains as label-free/transductive. The HF model card still calls the manuscript 'in preparation' while the repository links arXiv 2606.11508. The release notes also list an NGC download, which was not verified. Preprints only; weights not executed.

catalog_upserts.name: AceFF
catalog_upserts.description: Family of machine-learned interatomic potentials from Acellera for drug-like small molecules, including charged states (TensorNet in AceFF-1.x, TensorNet2 in AceFF-2); the AceFF-2-RESP-1 variant also predicts per-atom RESP charges for electrostatically embedded NNP/MM simulations.
catalog_upserts.status: Public ungated weights on Hugging Face, Apache-2.0 declared in the model cards (no LICENSE file in the AceFF-2.0 and RESP repos); inference code TorchMD-Net (MIT), RESP variant needs an unmerged branch; training data proprietary, not released; no hosted API
catalog_upserts.io: 3D small-molecule structure (elements H, B, C, N, O, F, Si, P, S, Cl, Br, I) with total charge -2 to +2 -> energy and forces (RESP variant: also per-atom RESP charges)
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Small-molecule MD, torsion scans, geometry optimisation, NNP/MM and relative binding free energy workflows
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Vendor-authored preprints (Acellera; authors declare competing interests). Training data are an in-house proprietary DFT set (about 12M conformations) and are not released. AceFF-2.0 and AceFF-2-RESP-1 cards declare Apache-2.0, but their license_link points to a LICENSE file that returns 404; the AceFF-1.0/1.1 repos include the Apache-2.0 LICENSE and NOTICE. RESP inference needs the unmerged torchmd-net resp_model branch; the RBFE embedding code is an Acellera/atm branch under LGPL-3.0. Year follows the first public AceFF-1.0 release (QuantumBind-RBFE preprint January 2025; Hugging Face repo February 2025). Weights not executed.

catalog_upserts.name: MACE-OFF
catalog_upserts.description: Transferable short-range MACE machine-learning force fields for neutral, closed-shell organic systems of ten elements (H, C, N, O, F, P, S, Cl, Br, I), trained on SPICE quantum-chemical reference data; released as MACE-OFF23 small/medium/large and MACE-OFF24 medium and applied to gas- and condensed-phase organic simulation, torsion scans and solvated peptide and small-protein MD.
catalog_upserts.status: MACE code MIT; public ungated model files on GitHub under the Academic Software Licence (reciprocal; academic non-commercial use at educational, non-profit or governmental institutions only); training data MIT; no API
catalog_upserts.io: 3D atomic coordinates and element types of neutral organic molecules, liquids or molecular crystals (10 elements) -> potential energy and forces
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Organic and biomolecular MD, torsion scans, molecular crystals and liquids, free-energy surfaces in explicit solvent, starting point for fine-tuning
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Model files under the Academic Software Licence (non-commercial, academic institutions only, reciprocal); MACE code MIT; training data MIT per its DataCite record. MACE-OFF24(M) is described in the paper (arXiv v5, JACS); MACE-OFF23b medium appears only in the v0.2 repo release note. Short-range models without explicit long-range electrostatics, for neutral closed-shell systems of 10 elements. The ACS landing page blocks automated fetch (403); content checked via Crossref and the PMC open-access copy. Weights listed, not downloaded or executed.

catalog_upserts.name: GRACE-OFF
catalog_upserts.description: Graph Atomic Cluster Expansion (GRACE) machine-learned interatomic potentials in one- and two-layer, small/medium/large variants. They are trained on the SPICE v2.0 subset of neutral molecules containing H, C, N, O, F, P, S, Cl, Br and I. Benchmarks cover energies and forces, torsion profiles, condensed-phase properties of organic liquids and water, and MD stability of gas-phase Ala15 and solvated crambin.
catalog_upserts.status: Public ungated model files in the GitHub repository (repository licence MIT; the repository also redistributes third-party MACE-OFF model files, which are under the Academic Software Licence upstream). Running the models requires the GRACE tensorpotential/gracemaker library under the Academic Software Licence (academic non-commercial use only). Training data on Zenodo under CC BY 4.0. No hosted API.
catalog_upserts.io: 3D coordinates of neutral organic molecules or liquids (elements H, C, N, O, F, P, S, Cl, Br, I) -> energies and forces
catalog_upserts.use_cases: MD of organic liquids and water, torsion scans, condensed-phase property prediction; biomolecular MD (stability shown for gas-phase Ala15 and solvated crambin)
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Identity: the paper's Data Availability points to heid-lab/grace-off (owned by the corresponding author's lab). The models/1l and models/2l b_off_{small,medium,large} directories match the paper's Table 1 hyperparameters. The repo has no tagged release and also holds a_wpS variants that the paper does not describe. The repository licence is MIT, but it also redistributes MACE-OFF model files (ASL upstream) without an ASL notice. The documented inference route (tensorpotential TPCalculator) is ASL, academic non-commercial only, hence noncommercial=true. Training data on Zenodo, CC BY 4.0. Neutral species and 10 elements only; biomolecular evidence is MD stability on two systems. The publisher page returns 403 to scripted clients; full text was read via PMC and Europe PMC. Not executed.

catalog_upserts.name: Atom-JEPA
catalog_upserts.description: Self-supervised joint-embedding predictive (JEPA) pretraining for 3D atomistic structures, released as two EquiformerV3 context encoders (39M parameters each): one pretrained on ~19M Uni-Mol molecules and one on ~1.7M Alexandria inorganic crystals, for fine-tuning or frozen feature extraction.
catalog_upserts.status: Open code (MIT; pip package atom-jepa) + public ungated encoder weights (molecules, crystals) on Hugging Face under CC BY 4.0; pretraining data are third-party (Uni-Mol, Alexandria) and not redistributed; no hosted API.
catalog_upserts.io: Atomic numbers + 3D coordinates (molecules from SMILES via a generated RDKit conformer; crystals with lattice) -> per-atom equivariant features and 256-d structure embeddings
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Molecular ADMET and quantum-chemical property prediction, frozen 3D molecular embeddings; crystal (materials) property prediction
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Preprint only (arXiv v1, 2026-10-06), not peer reviewed. Paper links both the GitHub repository and the Hugging Face repository; the 'atom-jepa' HF organisation lists three of the paper's authors as members. HF API lists molecules/ and crystals/ model.safetensors, ungated, CC BY 4.0; code MIT. Not related to Mol-JEPA. Weights not downloaded or executed.

catalog_upserts.name: ether0
catalog_upserts.description: 24-billion-parameter chemistry reasoning language model post-trained from Mistral-Small-24B-Instruct-2501 without additional domain pretraining: supervised fine-tuning on reasoning traces, then reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards on 640,730 chemistry problems (18 task types, 375 subtasks); reasons in English and answers with a molecule as SMILES.
catalog_upserts.status: Open weights on Hugging Face (Apache-2.0, ungated); code repository (Apache-2.0) holds reward functions and data utilities, no training code; 325-question test benchmark CC BY 4.0
catalog_upserts.io: Natural-language chemistry question (optionally containing SMILES) -> reasoning trace and a SMILES answer
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Constrained molecule design and editing (solubility, pKa, scent, receptor activity, ADME, GHS toxicity, blood-brain barrier), one-step retrosynthesis, reaction outcome prediction, name/description-to-SMILES, natural-product structure proposal from formula and organism; not a property-value predictor or general chat model
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Post-trained general LLM (no domain pretraining); in scope by precedent of TxGemma and BioReason-Pro, with chemistry scope comparable to ChemDFM. Released weights are the safety-post-trained model; the model card states its benchmarks differ from the preprint's pre-safety numbers. Model card: not a general chat model, weak textbook knowledge, limited IUPAC support. 21 safetensors shards, about 94 GB, listed via the Hub API, not downloaded or run. Training problems not found as a released dataset (paper says sources are public and prompt templates are open-sourced). Crossref also lists a NeurIPS 2025 proceedings version, DOI 10.52202/085713-5269.

catalog_upserts.name: PertMind
catalog_upserts.description: Biological reasoning language model: Qwen3-4B-Base post-trained with LoRA, first by one epoch of supervised fine-tuning on filtered model-generated reasoning traces, then by GRPO reinforcement learning whose gene-, pathway- and format-level rewards come from measured drug responses in the Tahoe-100M single-cell perturbation atlas.
catalog_upserts.status: Apache-2.0 ungated weights, tokenizer and inference scripts on Hugging Face; GitHub is an Apache-2.0 landing page with no source code (the paper says code is there); training code and the derived training corpus not released (source atlas Tahoe-100M is public); no hosted API
catalog_upserts.io: Text query (cell line, small-molecule perturbation, target gene, with retrieved biological context) -> reasoning trace and Up/Down/No expression-change call; free-text gene profiles, which the paper turns into gene, cell and donor embeddings using OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002 and task-specific projections
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Drug-induced gene-expression response prediction in unseen cell lines; reverse inference of the perturbation behind a cell-state change, including CRISPRa/i and double genetic perturbations; briefs that help other LLMs prioritise phenotypic-screen hits and name gene-set processes; text profiles for gene, cell and donor representations
catalog_upserts.audit_note: arXiv preprint only; no peer-reviewed version found. v2 (22 Aug 2026) was withdrawn with the comment that one or more co-authors did not consent to posting and that no replacement would be submitted; v3 (6 Oct 2026) came from a different submitting author, lists 19 authors instead of 11, and points to the same GitHub and Hugging Face artifacts (HF files unchanged since 17 Aug 2026; HF account name matches the first author). Post-training is LoRA (rank 64) on a single task, forward drug-response calls; breadth rests on the authors' zero-shot transfer results, two of which use PertMind output to assist other LLMs, and the representation results need an external OpenAI embedding model. The authors state that the Figure 1 capability space is broader than the evaluated subset. Hub file listing, Apache-2.0 card and LICENSE, and base-model licence (Qwen3-4B-Base, Apache-2.0) inspected; weights not downloaded or run; Tahoe-100M data terms not checked.

catalog_upserts.name: InstructCell
catalog_upserts.description: Instruction-following single-cell language model from the ZJUNLP group: a Q-Former feeds scRNA-seq profiles into a T5-base backbone and a conditional VAE decodes generated expression profiles. Instruction-tuned, without large-scale unlabeled single-cell pretraining, on 299,155 human and mouse cells from ten public datasets; released as chat and instruct checkpoints.
catalog_upserts.status: Open code + weights: MIT code on GitHub; ungated chat and instruct checkpoints on Hugging Face, MIT stated in card metadata only, loadable only with the GitHub code and its gene vocabulary; backbone T5-base is Apache-2.0. Training data not redistributed (public sources, rebuilt via notebooks); no hosted API
catalog_upserts.io: Natural-language instruction + scRNA-seq profile (h5ad mapped to the released 18,961-gene vocabulary) -> cell-type label or drug resistant/sensitive call, with optional explanatory text (chat version); text-specified conditions (cell type, tissue, species) -> generated pseudo-cell expression profile
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Natural-language single-cell analysis: cell-type annotation, conditional pseudo-cell generation, drug-sensitivity prediction
catalog_upserts.audit_note: arXiv preprint only (2501.08187v2); no journal version found in Europe PMC or Crossref title searches. Authors state it does not rely on large-scale unlabeled pre-training: T5-base instruction-tuned with new Q-Former/CVAE modules on ten public human and mouse datasets, so it sits at the scope boundary and follows the ChatCell precedent. Outputs reflect training-set label sets; zero-shot use is future work in the paper. Hub weights carry MIT in card metadata only and need the GitHub code. Weights not downloaded or executed.

catalog_upserts.name: Evolla
catalog_upserts.description: Protein-language generative model from Westlake University that links a frozen SaProt protein encoder to a frozen Llama 3-family language decoder through trainable compressor and aligner modules; trained on 546 million protein-text pairs to answer natural-language questions about proteins from sequence and Foldseek structure tokens; released at 10B and 80B scale.
catalog_upserts.status: MIT code; ungated Hugging Face weights labelled MIT (10B, 10B-DPO and Transformers-format -hf variants; 80B as split archive parts with no usage documentation) plus an author-run web chat server; the frozen decoders are Meta Llama 3 8B-Instruct (10B) and Llama 3.1 70B-Instruct (80B), whose Meta community licences are gated upstream and not reconciled with the MIT label; training corpus not released
catalog_upserts.io: Protein sequence + Foldseek structure tokens (80B also accepts sequence-only input) + natural-language question -> free-text answer about protein function
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Protein function question answering, functional annotation, interactive protein exploration
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Older release absent from the baseline, found in the 2026-10-10 multimodal sweep. Year follows the Evolla-10B Hub release (6 Dec 2024); the preprint (v4, Feb 2026) is not journal-published. Paper Methods name Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct (10B) and Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (80B) as frozen decoders; the HF cards' base_model tag says Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, which conflicts with the paper and README. Weights are labelled MIT and include Meta Llama decoder weights, with no Llama licence file; the original-repo route needs the gated Meta checkpoint. The 80B repo card holds only a licence tag and the repo has no 80B config. Weights not downloaded or executed.

catalog_upserts.name: nach0
catalog_upserts.description: Multi-domain, multi-task T5-architecture encoder-decoder language model (base 250M, large 780M parameters) pre-trained on chemistry-related PubMed abstracts, USPTO patents and ZINC molecule strings, then instruction-tuned on biomedical NLP and chemistry tasks; one model handles text, SMILES and cross-domain text-molecule generation.
catalog_upserts.status: Ungated base (Transformers) and large (NeMo) weights on Hugging Face under CC BY-NC 4.0, which the model card restricts to research use; the official GitHub repository holds only a README with an inference snippet and carries no licence file; no training code released; non-commercial terms apply to at least one artifact or access route
catalog_upserts.io: Natural-language instruction with optional SMILES -> text answers, named entities, generated or transformed molecules, property predictions
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Biomedical question answering and NER, molecule generation, reaction and retrosynthesis prediction, molecular property prediction
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Older release absent from the baseline, found during the 2026-10-10 multimodal discovery sweep. The paper's Code availability section names the two Hugging Face checkpoints and github.com/insilicomedicine/nach0. That repository contains only a README (inference snippet) and has no licence file. Weights are tagged CC BY-NC 4.0, and the card limits them to research use. The card's dataset sentence (CC BY 4.0 described as non-commercial) contradicts itself, and no nach0 dataset is released. The RSC landing page behind the DOI blocks automated clients (403); journal identity confirmed via Crossref and Europe PMC (PMC11151847). Distinct from the follow-up nach0-pc (arXiv 2410.09240; hub repo empty). Weights not downloaded or executed.

catalog_upserts.name: gReLU
catalog_upserts.description: Genentech's MIT-licensed Python framework for training, evaluating, interpreting and applying DNA sequence-to-function models, with a public Hugging Face model zoo of reusable checkpoints (Decima, gReLU-format conversions of Enformer and Borzoi, and several Genentech task models) plus their training data and lineage metadata.
catalog_upserts.status: MIT code; model-zoo checkpoints and datasets public on Hugging Face (ungated, cards labelled MIT; Enformer and Borzoi checkpoints are Genentech conversions of the published third-party weights); the zoo's Decima card directs loading through the separate decima package under the Genentech Non-Commercial Software License, so non-commercial terms apply to at least one access route
catalog_upserts.io: DNA sequence (+ genomic tracks or labels for training) -> trained or zoo sequence-to-function models, track predictions, attributions, variant-effect scores, designed sequences
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Building and benchmarking DNA sequence models, variant effect prediction, regulatory grammar interpretation, regulatory element design, reuse of Enformer/Borzoi/Decima checkpoints
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Platform/framework record, not a model. Paper describes the zoo on Weights & Biases; README v1.1.0 says it moved to Hugging Face (legacy W&B API slated for removal). Zoo cards and datasets are labelled MIT; Enformer/Borzoi checkpoints are Genentech conversions of third-party weights whose upstream code is Apache-2.0 (upstream weight terms not re-audited), and Decima's own package is Genentech Non-Commercial, so per-checkpoint terms should be read from the original model records. noncommercial=true because the documented Decima access route uses the non-commercial decima package. Year follows the 2024 bioRxiv preprint (journal 2025). No checkpoint downloaded or executed.

catalog_upserts.name: BioLLM
catalog_upserts.description: BGI framework that wraps several single-cell foundation models (scGPT, Geneformer, scFoundation, scBERT, CellPLM) behind one standardized API for zero-shot embedding, fine-tuning and benchmarking.
catalog_upserts.status: Platform/framework, no own pretrained model. Code: MIT top-level licence, but the repository vendors upstream model code (scBERT code from a GPL-3.0 repository; scFoundation code under Apache-2.0). Checkpoints: author Zenodo bundle labelled CC BY 4.0 that redistributes third-party weights (Geneformer, scBERT, scFoundation, scGPT; no CellPLM); upstream terms govern each, and the scFoundation weights are licensed for non-commercial research only
catalog_upserts.io: scRNA-seq expression matrix -> cell/gene embeddings and task outputs (cell-type annotation, gene regulatory networks, drug sensitivity) from the selected scFM
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Switching between and benchmarking scFMs, zero-shot cell embeddings, cell-type annotation, GRN inference, drug-sensitivity prediction
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Platform/framework record (Helical-like); identify by the Patterns DOI and the BGIResearch repository, since several unrelated projects share the name BioLLM. Terms are mixed: the repository is MIT at top level but copies the scBERT code tree (upstream GPL-3.0) without a GPL notice in that folder. The author Zenodo checkpoint bundle (record 14189969, 'Bio_tools', models.zip ~1.68 GB, not downloaded) carries a blanket CC BY 4.0 label, but its archive preview lists models/scfoundation/models.ckpt (1.4 GB, size-consistent with the upstream scFoundation checkpoint), whose upstream Model License is non-commercial and non-sublicensable; noncommercial=true on that basis. CellPLM is supported by a loader but its checkpoint is not in the bundle. Repository last pushed 2025-12-31; release v1.2.0 (2025-04-21); no execution test. Year follows the 2024-11-22 bioRxiv preprint.

catalog_upserts.name: scUnify
catalog_upserts.description: Framework that runs inference, fine-tuning (probing, partial or full fine-tuning, Hugging Face PEFT) and downstream tasks across five single-cell foundation models (Geneformer, scGPT, scFoundation, UCE, Nicheformer) while keeping each backbone's own environment and preprocessing; not a new model.
catalog_upserts.status: MIT code (source install, v0.1.0, no tagged release or PyPI package); no weights of its own. Setup downloads third-party checkpoints under their own terms: scFoundation weights are non-commercial research only (BioMap scFoundation Model License) and are fetched from the genbio-ai Hugging Face mirror, which states no licence; Geneformer Apache-2.0, Nicheformer MIT, UCE CC BY 4.0, scGPT from the authors' Google Drive (repo MIT).
catalog_upserts.io: AnnData scRNA-seq + model/task configuration -> cell embeddings, trained task heads and evaluation metrics across scFM backbones
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Comparing scFM backbones and adaptation strategies; cell-type classification on all five backbones; model-native regression (Nicheformer), batch correction (scGPT) and perturbation prediction (scGPT, scFoundation); connecting a custom trainable task to several backbones
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Preprint only (not peer reviewed); v1 (2026-03-03) carried a different title focused on zero-shot inference. Early-stage software: no PyPI package, no tagged release, single maintainer. Overlaps Helical/BioLLM functionality. noncommercial=true because the scFoundation checkpoint that setup downloads is under BioMap's non-commercial Model License; scUnify's own notices list scFoundation only as Apache-2.0 (code). The scFoundation checkpoint comes from the genbio-ai Hugging Face upload, not BioMap's own link. Paper quotes obtained through a WebFetch extraction of the bioRxiv full text. No execution test. Same-name collision: github.com/hungms/scUnify (2024) is unrelated.

catalog_upserts.name: BioPipelines
catalog_upserts.description: University of Zurich Python framework that chains structure-generation, sequence-design, structure-prediction, docking and analysis tools (over 40 in the CSBJ paper, 70+ in current docs; e.g. RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN, AlphaFold, Boltz-2) into multistep workflows; the same script runs interactively in Jupyter/Colab or as generated batch jobs on HPC clusters. It orchestrates separately installed tools and does not host models.
catalog_upserts.status: Open MIT framework code; no hosted service and no bundled weights. Integrated tools and their weights are installed from upstream and keep their own licences (including GPL/LGPL components)
catalog_upserts.io: Python workflow script + protein/ligand inputs (PDB structures, sequences, SMILES) -> generated bash jobs run in Jupyter/Colab or on SLURM/LSF/PBS clusters, producing designed structures and sequences plus result tables
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Inverse folding, de novo protein design, compound library screening, iterative binding-site optimization, fusion-protein linker optimization, codon-optimised gene design
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Workflow-orchestration platform, not a model: it generates batch scripts for separately installed third-party tools. MIT licence confirmed by the GitHub licence API and the CSBJ abstract (DOI 10.34133/csbj.0129). noncommercial=false covers the framework only. A GitHub licence spot-check of 46 linked tool repos found no non-commercial repo licence but did find copyleft (PLIP, Open Babel GPL-2.0; VespaG GPL-3.0; xtb LGPL-3.0). Weight terms of most integrated models were not audited. The publisher DOI landing returns 403 to scripted access, so PMC is used. Unrelated GitHub repos share the name BioPipelines; the official one is locbp-uzh/biopipelines. No install or execution test.

catalog_upserts.name: IDiom
catalog_upserts.description: Autoregressive protein language model family (18.9M, 85M and 302M parameters) trained on IDiom-DB, 54 million predicted intrinsically disordered regions curated from the AlphaFold Database, which generates IDRs with or without flanking protein context through a fill-in-the-middle format and also exposes layer-wise IDR embeddings and post-training. A Top-K sparse autoencoder on layer 18 of the 302M model (16,384 latents, k=32) is released alongside for feature analysis and steered generation.
catalog_upserts.status: Open code + weights (MIT code and model weights; IDiom-DB corpus CC BY 4.0)
catalog_upserts.io: Flanking protein context in fill-in-the-middle format or an empty prompt -> generated intrinsically disordered region sequences; IDR sequences or annotated FASTA -> per-residue or pooled layer embeddings and 16,384-dimensional layer-18 SAE features used for conditioning
catalog_upserts.use_cases: De novo and context-conditioned IDR design, IDR embedding extraction for downstream modelling, post-training (supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning with custom rewards), interpretable SAE-feature steering of generated regions
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Adversarial re-verification 2026-10-10: arXiv 2610.02189 re-fetched via the arXiv API (submitted 2026-10-01, abstract names IDiom and IDiom-DB and the GitHub repo); rotskoff-group/idiom confirmed non-fork, MIT via the GitHub licence endpoint and LICENSE body, release v1.0.0 dated 2026-10-02 with no binary assets; hub repos idiom-20M / idiom-85M / idiom-300M and idiomsae-300M-L18-k32 all gated=false with cardData.license=mit and inspected file listings (model.safetensors, sae.safetensors); dataset jxliu2/idiom-db cc-by-4.0, ungated, 54,155,136 records across three splits. An earlier IDiom release (v0.0.0) corresponds to the workshop preprint DOI 10.64898/2026.04.10.717777, confirmed through Crossref, and is the same model line rather than a separate record. Scope is deliberately narrow to disordered regions; reusability rests on released weights plus documented generation, embedding and post-training routes. No weights were downloaded or executed; the CC BY 4.0 corpus term is the depositors' declaration over AFDB/UniProt-derived data.

catalog_upserts.name: ProteinSage
catalog_upserts.description: Protein language model from BioMap Research and Peking University. Pretraining adds AlphaFold DB-predicted residue-proximity priors through structure-guided masking and a structural causal objective over spatially close residue pairs; inference takes sequence only. The released 650M checkpoint provides representations for structure-aware and general protein tasks.
catalog_upserts.status: Apache-2.0 code; one ungated ProteinSage-650M checkpoint on Hugging Face under CC BY-NC 4.0 (77M/150M paper models not published); downstream data CC BY 4.0 on Zenodo; non-commercial terms apply to the weights
catalog_upserts.io: Protein sequence -> per-residue hidden states (embeddings) and attention maps; per the card the masked-LM output layer may load newly initialised
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Protein representation extraction and fine-tuning (structure, function, localization tasks); embedding-based family screening, as in the paper's adapter-based microbial rhodopsin prioritization
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Adversarial review 2026-10-10. bioRxiv v2 (2026-09-09) Code Availability names the GitHub repo (tag v1.0.1) and the Hugging Face checkpoint. The hub config matches the paper's 650M architecture. The hub repo is ungated with pytorch_model.bin listed. Weights are CC BY-NC 4.0 (card metadata plus LICENSE on the hub and in the repo), code is Apache-2.0 and Zenodo data is CC BY 4.0. Only the 650M checkpoint is published. The ProteinSage-Miner adapter used for the rhodopsin screen was not found among the released artifacts. A token-gated ModelScope route in scripts/ was not checked. No weights were downloaded or run, and benchmark and rhodopsin results were not reproduced.

catalog_upserts.name: ProteomeLM
catalog_upserts.description: Proteome-scale language model that reads an entire proteome at once, taking each protein's ESM-C embedding, together with an OrthoDB orthologous-group encoding, as a token so that representations carry whole-proteome context. Four pretrained sizes (5.7M-328M) are released, with task heads for protein-protein interaction and gene-essentiality prediction.
catalog_upserts.status: Apache-2.0 code; four public ungated Hugging Face checkpoints (XS-L) with no licence declared on their model repositories; Apache-2.0 essentiality head; training dataset public on Hugging Face with no licence declared; inference requires ESM-C 600M embeddings under their own terms
catalog_upserts.io: Whole proteome as a protein FASTA -> proteome-context protein embeddings, protein-protein interaction scores and per-protein essentiality probabilities
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Proteome-context protein representation, protein-protein interaction prediction, gene essentiality prediction, host-pathogen interaction fine-tuning (repository LoRA code; no released host-pathogen checkpoint)
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Older model met during the October sweep and absent from the baseline; the in-window event is the 2026-09-30 Apache-2.0 essentiality head and repository release 1.1 (2026-09-29/30). The PNAS landing page returns HTTP 403 to automated fetches; journal identity is from Crossref and the open PMC full text (PMC13214046), whose availability statement points to the GitHub repository for code and weights. The four base checkpoints are public and ungated but declare no licence on their model repositories (no model card), so noncommercial=false is not evidence of permissive weight terms; the training-dataset repository likewise has no licence metadata. Host-pathogen fine-tuning is repository code added in release 1.1 and is not part of the PNAS article; no fine-tuned host-pathogen checkpoint is released. Running the model depends on ESM-C 600M embeddings (biohub card currently MIT/other). No weights were downloaded or executed; year follows the 2025-08-03 preprint.

catalog_upserts.name: AAMFM
catalog_upserts.description: Antigen-conditioned antibody foundation model built on the open ESM3 1.4B backbone: antibody-domain continual pretraining on paired sequence-structure data, then adapter-based supervised fine-tuning that fuses antigen geometric features with epitope annotations, then calibrated DPO alignment, for antibody sequence-structure co-design conditioned on a target antigen.
catalog_upserts.status: Code MIT; ungated MIT checkpoint on Hugging Face (AAMFM.pt), though the repository README limits MIT to the source code and leaves pretrained weights, external datasets and third-party tools to their own terms. Inference additionally needs the external ESM3 open 1.4B weights and structure/function codec files (ESM repository and hub card both state MIT, ungated) and, for the bundled RAbD evaluation, a precomputed GearNet antigen-feature file on Google Drive with no stated licence. Training data external and not provided.
catalog_upserts.io: Antigen structure with epitope-site annotations plus antibody framework sequences -> designed CDR sequences and a complete antibody structure
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Antigen-specific antibody and CDR-H3 design, antibody sequence-structure co-design conditioned on a target epitope
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Independently re-verified 2026-10-10 against arXiv 2607.20057v1, the official MIT repository (owner at SJTU, 'Official implementation', bidirectional link with the hub card) and the ungated hub repository GENTEL-Lab/AAMFM, whose file listing shows AAMFM.pt (5,627,577,098 bytes, LFS sha256 4795a7bd...). No weights downloaded or executed, no design validated. Limits: the card does not say which training stage the single checkpoint is (CPT, SFT or Cal-DPO); the repository README's MIT statement covers code only and defers pretrained weights, external datasets and third-party tools to their own terms, which is narrower than the hub card's MIT statement for the checkpoint; the required external ESM3 assets were checked this time and are MIT and ungated (evolutionaryscale/esm LICENSE.md is MIT; EvolutionaryScale/esm3-sm-open-v1 redirects to biohub/esm3-sm-open-v1, ungated, card states MIT), so no non-commercial term was found on any route; the Google Drive GearNet antigen-feature file and the external training data carry no stated terms. Evaluation covers two antibody design settings (de novo sequence-structure co-design and epitope-binding CDR-H3 co-design), so breadth sits near the inclusion boundary; pseudo-log-likelihood scoring in the paper and repository is computed by the third-party AntiBERTy model, not by AAMFM, and is therefore not listed as an AAMFM output.

catalog_upserts.name: Trias
catalog_upserts.description: BART-style encoder-decoder codon language model (about 47M parameters) trained on 10 million mRNA coding sequences from 640 vertebrate species in NCBI RefSeq, which reverse-translates a protein sequence into a species-conditioned codon sequence. Zero-shot sequence likelihoods from the model correlate with measured mRNA stability and protein output in the authors' evaluations. A smaller mammalian-only variant without the species tag (about 12.3M parameters) is released as Trias-Small.
catalog_upserts.status: Open code (MIT) + ungated weights (MIT) for two checkpoints; install from source, no tagged release; training corpus not redistributed (RefSeq-derived)
catalog_upserts.io: Protein sequence, with a species tag for Trias and without one for Trias-Small -> generated codon sequence (greedy, beam or nucleus decoding) and model likelihood scores usable zero-shot
catalog_upserts.use_cases: mRNA codon optimisation and design, species-specific reverse translation, zero-shot scoring of candidate coding sequences against mRNA stability and protein output
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Adversarially re-verified 2026-10-10 against the primary sources. Preprint versions: v1 2025-05-13, v2 2025-06-06, v3 2026-10-05 (CC BY 4.0, no journal version recorded in the bioRxiv API). Year 2025 reflects first public release; the v3 preprint and the Trias-Small checkpoint (created 2026-10-01) are the current artifacts. MIT is declared in the repository LICENSE (Copyright (c) 2025 Lareau Lab) and in the YAML of both hub cards; both checkpoints are gated=false. Limits: (1) the paper's Code availability statement names only github.com/lareaulab/Trias and huggingface.co/lareaulab/Trias - Trias-Small is treated as author-endorsed because it sits under the same lareaulab account, cross-links the main card, and matches the paper's 'Trias-small' architecture description, but it is not named in the paper; (2) checkpoints were listed via the hub API, never downloaded or loaded, so weight integrity is unverified; (3) no tagged release exists, so there is no version-pinned artifact; (4) the training corpus is not redistributed (data.zip in the repo holds figure and benchmark data only); (5) the reported expression advantages are the authors' own wet-lab results - H.B. and M.F. hold equity in TriasBio, Inc., L.F.L. is an advisor, and the company funded the experimental validation; the disclosure carries no licence restriction. Trias-Small is recorded as an alias of the same family because it shares paper, code and terms.

catalog_upserts.name: mRNA-GPT (Kitasato)
catalog_upserts.description: Family of decoder-only codon language models (302,109,696 parameters, 24 layers, 1024-dim, 16 heads, 68-token vocabulary of 64 codons plus special tokens), pretrained separately on bacterial, eukaryotic and archaeal coding sequences from NCBI RefSeq (about 80M, 83M and 2M CDSs). The released code implements synonymous-codon-constrained decoding, so generation can be conditioned on a target protein, and three property fine-tunes (bacterial expression, fungal expression, mRNA stability) are published from the same backbones.
catalog_upserts.status: Open code + weights, ungated. Code Apache-2.0 (LICENSE file in the repository); weights apache-2.0 as declared in each model card's metadata, with no separate licence file in the weight repositories. Three pretrained domain checkpoints plus three property fine-tunes, all downloadable without an account; no API route and no released training corpus (the corpus is rebuilt from NCBI RefSeq with the repository scripts). The preprint text is CC BY-NC 4.0; that covers the article, not the model.
catalog_upserts.io: Target protein or codon prompt -> generated coding sequence under synonymous-codon constraints, or codon-level embeddings
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Coding-sequence design and codon optimisation per domain of life, expression- and stability-oriented fine-tuning, codon-level representation learning
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Independently re-verified 2026-10-10. Ownership chain: the preprint's availability statement names only the code repository; that repository's owner is the paper's co-first author (GitHub account name ZHANG YIMING) and its README links the six Hugging Face checkpoints under the account ZYMScott (profile name 'yiming'), which is the author endorsement relied on here - the preprint itself does not mention Hugging Face. Checkpoints were published 2026-10-02, after the December 2025 preprint, and differ from the preprint's Methods in three details: context 2048 codons in config.json versus a 1,024-token window in the paper, rotary versus learnable positional encoding, and a 68-token vocabulary with BOS/EOS versus the paper's 69 items with CLS/SEP/MASK. Protein-constrained decoding is implemented and documented in the released code and model cards, while the preprint describes codon-constrained generation as future work. Three further ungated Apache-2.0 fine-tunes exist in the same namespace (bacterial-expression, fungal-expression, stability). The repository BibTeX entry has doi = {TODO}; the preprint DOI resolves and bioRxiv records no journal publication. A different, unrelated model is also called mRNA-GPT (Sanofi, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.03.31.715707, posted 2026-04-02), so the name is qualified and the bare alias is deliberately omitted. Files were listed by API, not downloaded or loaded; no inference was run, so reported behaviour is documentation, not reproduction.

catalog_upserts.name: La-Ribo
catalog_upserts.description: Generative flow-matching model for joint RNA sequence and three-dimensional structure design: it samples a sparse phosphate-sugar-base scaffold together with residue-wise latents, and a shared scaffold-conditioned autoencoder decodes nucleotide identities and all heavy atoms. Two released flow checkpoints (with and without triangle pair updates) share that autoencoder prior, which the paper also uses for scaffold-conditioned inverse folding without additional training.
catalog_upserts.status: Open code + weights (MIT), ungated; two flow checkpoints, shared autoencoder and normalisation statistics, plus a 10,631-structure predicted-structure dataset. Released scripts perform unconditional sampling only.
catalog_upserts.io: Target RNA length -> generated RNA sequence with all-heavy-atom 3D coordinates (PDB); scaffold conditioning is a paper protocol over the same weights, not a released script
catalog_upserts.use_cases: RNA sequence-structure co-design; generation of RNA structural candidates for downstream refolding or designability evaluation; scaffold-conditioned inverse folding as documented in the paper (user-implemented, same checkpoints, no retraining)
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Independently re-verified 2026-10-10, two days after the preprint and both repositories appeared, so the release is very new and unreplicated (GitHub: one commit, 4 stars, no releases; HF: 13 downloads). MIT is declared in the GitHub LICENSE ('Copyright (c) 2025 La-Ribo contributors') and in the HF card metadata and footer; HF gated=false. Weight files were listed by the HF API, never downloaded or executed. Released code performs unconditional sampling only; the README states it does not run inverse folding, refolding or the designability evaluation. The released data are the 10,631 trRosettaRNA2-predicted structures (bpRNA-1m90 and RNAStrAlign sequences) with per-residue pLDDT, not the 168,561-structure training corpus, which is not released and which the authors say consists mostly of predicted or synthetic structures; they also report that only 0.31% of the corpus exceeds 160 nt and that strict success declines toward the top of the 40-150 nt benchmark. Designability, codesignability and inverse-folding figures are the authors' own, against their chosen baselines (gRNAde, NA-MPNN, RiboFlow-Mix) and two refolding models. Not checked: upstream licence terms of the folding models (trRosettaRNA2, OpenFold3, NuFold) whose predictions make up the corpus, and any peer review of the preprint.

catalog_upserts.name: LucaCell
catalog_upserts.description: Sequence-centric single-cell foundation model that represents genes by frozen LucaOne mRNA-sequence embeddings instead of a fixed gene-ID vocabulary; a roughly 3B-parameter Transformer encoder pretrained by masked expression-bin modelling on about 85 million human and mouse cells.
catalog_upserts.status: Ungated public weights on Hugging Face whose model-card text states Apache-2.0, but the hub registers no licence; the GitHub code repository has no licence file (all rights reserved by default); downstream data, embeddings and task checkpoints on Zenodo under CC BY 4.0; pretraining corpus only at a temporary IP-address link with no stated licence
catalog_upserts.io: Binned single-cell expression + per-gene mRNA-sequence embeddings -> cell embeddings, masked expression-bin reconstruction and downstream predictions
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Cross-species and cross-modal (scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq) cell-type annotation without manual gene mapping, cell embedding, alignment-free microbial-read embedding, sequence-aware perturbation and SNP-aware expression prediction, influenza viral-load prediction
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Preprint only (bioRxiv, posted 14 Sep 2026). GitHub code has no LICENSE (API licence null, /license 404). Hub card states Apache-2.0, but stray text precedes its YAML block, so the hub records no licence. Paper says ~3B parameters; card says ~3.15B. Card table names encoder LucaGroup/LucaOne-step60M (HTTP 401); config.json gene_embed_source is the public MIT LucaGroup/LucaOne-LucaCell-step60M, and lucaone_embedding.py hard-codes an internal local model path that users must edit. Pretraining corpus only at a temporary IP link. Not downloaded or executed.

catalog_upserts.name: CellMSA
catalog_upserts.description: Single-cell representation model that retrieves related cells across batches and cell types as MSA-like context and feeds context-derived gene-pair features to a pair-aware cell encoder (GenePairformer); pretrained on about 109 million human CELLxGENE cell observations (65.6 million primary).
catalog_upserts.status: Open code + weights in one GitHub repo under MIT licence text with third-party notices (GitHub: NOASSERTION); checkpoint via Git LFS; no separate weights licence; paper recommends research-only use; no API
catalog_upserts.io: AnnData scRNA-seq expression (Ensembl gene IDs) + reference AnnData with precomputed context-cell indices (shipped preparation script uses cell-type/donor/supertype annotations) -> cell embeddings
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Batch integration, cell type and state classification, embeddings for downstream perturbation prediction
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Discovery 2026-10-10. arXiv preprint v1 (2026-09-30); arXiv comment says 'Accepted by NeurIPS 2026' (author-stated, UNVERIFIED). Repo LICENSE is MIT text plus third-party attribution (GitHub NOASSERTION) and covers the in-repo checkpoint; the paper's Broader Impacts recommends research-only use (not a licence term). The 566 MB checkpoint is a Git LFS object (LFS batch API and HEAD 200; LFS bandwidth limits may apply). Inference needs an NVIDIA GPU and precomputed context indices; the shipped context script and demo are label-informed, and the paper's label-free KNN retrieval is not shipped as a script. The main integration benchmark used label-informed context while baselines did not; the label-free comparison covers Bladder only. Not executed.

catalog_upserts.name: scMaize
catalog_upserts.description: Maize-specific single-cell foundation models: two 6-layer Transformer encoders (expression-only scMaizeExp, 16.7M parameters; Gene Ontology-informed scMaizeGO, 16.8M) pretrained by masked gene modelling on the 385,675-cell scMaizeAtlas (20 projects, seven tissues), released with an online atlas and analysis apps.
catalog_upserts.status: MIT-licensed code on GitHub; ungated pretrained checkpoints downloadable from the project website with no licence stated (all rights reserved by default); atlas data on the website without stated terms; free web apps without login
catalog_upserts.io: Maize scRNA-seq expression (h5ad; genes matched to a 15,000-gene vocabulary, 2,048 gene tokens per cell) -> 384-dim cell embeddings, masked-gene expression predictions; cell-type and tissue labels via fine-tuning or the web annotation app
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Maize cell-type annotation and tissue classification, embedding-based clustering and batch-aware integration, expression imputation, zero-/few-shot cross-species cell-type classification (tested on rice and Arabidopsis), root stress/perturbation-state analysis
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Preprint only (bioRxiv v1 5 Aug, v2 3 Sep 2026; preprint text CC BY-NC-ND 4.0). Small single-species corpus. Checkpoints are served from the project website (HEAD 200: 78,947,888 and 102,583,738 bytes; not downloaded), not a hub or archive, with no weight licence; site names scMaizeExp.pt/scMaizeGO.pt while the repo README names *_best.pt with matching sizes. The README's 21.6 GB pretraining pickle is not in the website resource list. README clone URL is a placeholder.

catalog_upserts.name: CELL-FM (virtual microscopy)
catalog_upserts.description: Bidirectional sequence-image generative model from the Huang lab (UCSF) that generates a protein's fluorescence microscopy image from its sequence and cellular context, and proposes sequences consistent with an image. Pretrained on about 1.1 million Human Protein Atlas single-cell images, with separate OpenCell and CondenSeq checkpoints.
catalog_upserts.status: Open code + weights (MIT; ungated Hugging Face checkpoints that bundle the ESM C 600M encoder, now MIT upstream); demo Space; generated-image dataset has no licence stated; training data under their own terms
catalog_upserts.io: Protein sequence + cell-context channels (nucleus; ER and microtubules for HPA; expression level for CondenSeq) -> protein fluorescence image; protein image + context -> protein sequence; image -> ViT embedding
catalog_upserts.use_cases: In silico protein localization, virtual staining atlases, NLS/NES screening and design, virtual mutagenesis and titration of condensate-forming peptides
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Preprint only (bioRxiv, 2026-09-18). Checkpoints are dataset-specific (HPA; OpenCell fine-tune for OpenCell proteins only; CondenSeq) and bundle ESM C 600M, whose current upstream card (biohub) lists MIT. The hub dataset of generated images has no licence (all rights reserved by default); HPA, OpenCell and CondenSeq terms not checked. Successor to CELL-Diff (not in catalog). Different model from CellFM (bfm-cellfm). Multimodal is an alternative modality. Not executed.

catalog_upserts.name: NexuST
catalog_upserts.description: Hierarchical spatial-transcriptomics foundation model that repeatedly interleaves gene-level molecular modelling with cell-level spatial modelling, pretrained by masked gene-value reconstruction on HumanST-46M (45.7 million human cells from 72 datasets on three imaging-based platforms across 11 organs).
catalog_upserts.status: Open MIT code; ungated Hugging Face checkpoint with no licence stated (all rights reserved by default); HumanST-46M pretraining data ungated on Hugging Face, also without a licence
catalog_upserts.io: Single-cell imaging-based spatial transcriptomics as AnnData (log-normalised expression, gene symbols in the model vocabulary, 2-D cell coordinates) -> cell embeddings; cell-type, region, held-out gene and neighbourhood-composition predictions through user-trained linear-probe or fine-tuned heads
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Spatial cell-type annotation, tissue-region prediction, held-out gene recovery, neighbourhood-composition prediction
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Preprint only. The paper names the GitHub and Hugging Face locators. The hub checkpoint is the step-10,000 state (the paper's full 10,000-step schedule); the card calls it an initial release, says it is not the best-validation-loss checkpoint, and documents no licence or verified loading example, while the GitHub inference, probe and fine-tuning commands target it. Same group and 46M-cell corpus as CellWorld (bfm-cellworld) but a distinct model (gene-value reconstruction, 67.9M parameters). Not executed.

catalog_upserts.name: stFormer
catalog_upserts.description: Transformer foundation model for spatial transcriptomics that adds biased cross-attention to ligand genes in each cell's spatial niche. Gene embeddings are initialised from scFoundation, and the model was pretrained on about 4.1 million samples obtained by cell-type deconvolution of public human Visium datasets.
catalog_upserts.status: Open code (MIT); pretrained and fine-tuned weights in a 9.3 GB Zenodo archive labelled MIT; building the model requires scFoundation weights (BioMap non-commercial research licence); pretraining corpus on request
catalog_upserts.io: Single-cell or spot expression plus ligand-gene expression from the spatial niche -> niche-aware gene embeddings and pooled cell embeddings
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Cell clustering and batch-effect correction, cell type prediction, gene function prediction, in silico ligand-receptor perturbation; case studies on spatial domain and signalling-ligand identification
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Code MIT. The README places pretrained weights, fine-tuned weights and formatted data in author Zenodo deposit 20755048 (open, labelled MIT, one 9.3 GB tarball); only the first archive entries were listed, so the checkpoint itself was not seen. Gene embeddings are initialised from scFoundation, and the official code loads the scFoundation checkpoint (downloaded separately; BioMap licence, non-commercial research only), hence noncommercial=true despite the MIT labels. Pretraining corpus available on request only. Several unrelated 'STFormer' models exist.

catalog_upserts.name: CROWN
aliases: Cytology visual foundation netwoRk Optimized With self-supervised learNing
catalog_upserts.description: Universal visual foundation model for computational cytopathology: a DINOv2-style ViT-L/16 encoder self-supervised on more than 10 million cytology image patches and evaluated across classification, segmentation, detection, retrieval and slide-level tasks.
catalog_upserts.status: Gated weights on Hugging Face (automatic approval after sharing contact details; hub metadata Apache-2.0); code on GitHub without a repository licence file (DINOv2-derived files keep Meta's Apache-2.0 headers, the authors' own scripts carry none); the paper limits code and weights to academic research purposes, so non-commercial terms apply to at least one access route
catalog_upserts.io: Cytology image patch (224 x 224) -> CLS-token embedding from the ViT-L/16 encoder, for linear probes, segmentation/detection heads or weakly supervised slide-level classification
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Patch-level classification of cervical, effusion, thyroid and blood cytology; thyroid and cervical segmentation and blood-cell detection; image retrieval; weakly supervised and few-shot slide-level classification
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Paper code-availability statement restricts code and weights to academic research, while HF hub metadata says Apache-2.0; the HF gate is the default contact-information gate (card text readable on the model page, raw README 401; no custom gate prompt in card metadata). GitHub has no LICENSE file; inherited DINOv2 files carry Meta Apache-2.0 headers, author scripts none. Paper read as abstract plus availability statements (full text paywalled); ViT-L/16 from README/model-card code. Year follows first public weights (HF 2026-01-21) and the 2026 paper; code was uploaded 2025-09-30; no preprint found.

catalog_upserts.name: ELF
catalog_upserts.description: Slide-level pathology encoder from the Li lab (Stanford): a multi-head gated attention-MIL aggregator pretrained with MoCo v3 contrastive learning and auxiliary weak supervision on 53,699 WSIs from 20 anatomical sites. It turns tile embeddings from five third-party pathology foundation models (UNI, CONCH v1.5, Prov-GigaPath, Virchow2, H-optimus-0) into slide-level representations, which are concatenated into one ensemble embedding.
catalog_upserts.status: Public code (GitHub) and ungated slide-encoder weights (an inference-only file on Hugging Face; the paper links a Google Drive training checkpoint). Both are described as GPLv3 with an added non-commercial academic-use restriction, and neither repository has a licence file. Inputs require five gated tile encoders, three of which (UNI, CONCH v1.5, Virchow2) are under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0
catalog_upserts.io: CLAM tile embeddings at 10x from UNI, CONCH v1.5, Prov-GigaPath, Virchow2 or H-optimus-0 -> per-model slide embedding (native dimension and 768-d) plus attention weights; the paper ensemble concatenates the five per-model slide embeddings
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Linear-probe cancer classification and subtyping, molecular biomarker detection, and prediction of response to chemotherapy, targeted therapy and immunotherapy in small cohorts
catalog_upserts.audit_note: The code and weights are labelled GPLv3 but also restricted to non-commercial academic use, which is internally inconsistent, and neither repository has a licence file; the record treats ELF as non-commercial. The paper states 14.3M parameters, but the Hugging Face inference encoder holds 151,304 (config.json). Its layers match the paper's Methods and the card calls it the trained momentum encoder, but I did not check that it is equivalent to the paper-linked Google Drive checkpoint, because that would mean downloading weights. ELF needs features from five gated third-party tile encoders. The Cancer Cell version was checked through Crossref, Europe PMC and the PMC full text (PMC13564370).

catalog_upserts.name: HEIST
aliases: Hierarchical Embeddings for Integrated Spatial Transcriptomics
catalog_upserts.description: Hierarchical graph transformer foundation model that represents tissue as a spatial cell graph whose nodes are per-cell gene co-expression graphs, producing cell- and gene-level embeddings; the paper's v1 checkpoint was pretrained on 22.3M cells from 124 tissue slices across 15 organs and reported to transfer to spatial proteomics without retraining. A v2.0 series added in October 2026 was retrained on a rebuilt corpus that, per the authors' model card, fixes a v1 preprocessing bug in which all cells of a cell type shared one expression vector.
catalog_upserts.status: Open code + weights: ungated MIT-labelled Hugging Face checkpoints (v1 at repo root; v2.0/marker_xenium); code repository has no licence file and its README states CC BY 4.0. The card's v2.0/marker_all (the code's default) and v2.0/nomarker_all were not uploaded as of 2026-10-10.
catalog_upserts.io: Spatial transcriptomics/proteomics cells as AnnData (raw counts + cell coordinates) -> cell and gene embeddings; v2.0 marker models keep only genes in a 6,495-symbol human vocabulary (mouse genes need ortholog mapping); preprocessing requires a CUDA GPU
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Cell clustering and spatially informed subpopulation discovery, cell-type annotation, gene imputation, clinical outcome prediction from tissue embeddings, transfer to spatial proteomics (reported for v1)
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Evidence and access reviewed 2026-10-10; see evidence/refresh-2026-10-10/candidate_decisions.json. arXiv code statement, GitHub README and HF card link each other; HF uploads by the first author. Weights metadata MIT, ungated; code has no licence file, README states CC BY 4.0. Author card discloses a v1 preprocessing bug (cells of a cell type shared one expression vector); arXiv v4 does not mention it, so paper results predate the fix. v2.0 release partial: only marker_xenium uploaded; code default v2.0/marker_all absent. ICLR 2026 venue UNVERIFIED (OpenReview not readable). Weights not downloaded or executed.

catalog_upserts.name: OpenMidnight
catalog_upserts.description: Sophont/MedARC open replication of kaiko.ai's Midnight training recipe: a 1.1B-parameter ViT-G/14 pathology tile encoder initialised from Meta's DINOv2 weights and further trained with DINOv2 self-supervision on about 12,000 public TCGA FFPE H&E slides, released with its full training pipeline.
catalog_upserts.status: Apache-2.0 code and Apache-2.0-labelled weights; weights sit behind an automatic Hugging Face gate asking for contact details, an institutional email and an attestation of affiliation and research use; the model card excludes clinical use; the training-patch mirror follows TCGA/GDC open-access terms
catalog_upserts.io: H&E histology tile (224 px) -> 1536-d tile-level embedding
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Patch-level tissue classification, slide-level classification from tile embeddings, nucleus segmentation probes, spatial gene-expression prediction from H&E (HEST), pathology feature-extraction backbone
catalog_upserts.audit_note: The primary document is a non-peer-reviewed Sophont technical report (14 Nov 2025), on the web and on Zenodo with DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20711012 (CC BY 4.0). No arXiv or peer-reviewed paper was found. The model card is publicly readable. The weight files are behind an automatic HF gate (institutional email, attestation of affiliation and research use) and were checked from the file listing, not downloaded. A maintainer-merged code fix (PR #77, Aug 2026) states that the released 250k checkpoint was trained with a sign-inverted KDE regulariser. Distinct from bfm-midnight-midnight-12k-midnight-92k (kaiko.ai weights); do not merge.

record.name: DeepSEA
record.description: Pioneering deep-learning sequence model that predicts 919 chromatin features (TF binding, DNase, histone marks) from DNA with single-nucleotide sensitivity to prioritize noncoding variants.
record.io: DNA sequence (~1 kb) -> 919 chromatin feature predictions; noncoding variant effect scores
record.status: HOLD: no written historical-exception policy; the original 2015 release host (deepsea.princeton.edu) was not serving DeepSEA on 2026-10-10; no licence was stated for the original download; successor Sei is catalogued as bfm-sei
record.use_cases: Noncoding/eQTL/disease variant prioritization, chromatin feature prediction, regulatory sequence analysis

code_links.label: Selene framework (DeepSEA architecture definition; not the original 2015 trained-model release)

record.name: ChromBPNet
record.description: Kundaje-lab bias-factorized, base-resolution CNN of chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq/DNase-seq), trained for each dataset. A frozen pretrained enzyme-bias model is combined with a trainable TF sub-model to reveal motif syntax, TF footprints and regulatory variant effects.
record.io: DNA sequence -> base-resolution accessibility profiles; TF motif/footprint and variant-effect outputs
record.status: HOLD: MIT code; CC-BY-4.0 reference bias models on Zenodo; per-dataset trained models on ENCODE/Synapse (terms there not checked); no single broadly pretrained model
record.use_cases: cis-regulatory syntax discovery, TF footprinting, regulatory variant scoring, enhancer/accessibility modeling
record.audit_note: Re-reviewed 2026-10-10 against preprint v4 (2026-09-23), README, licence, releases and the Zenodo bias-model deposit. Per-dataset predictor with a transferable bias component; no broad reusable pretraining and no scope policy for assay-specific predictors.

review.reason: Re-reviewed 2026-10-10. The preprint was revised to v4 (2026-09-23; still not journal-published) with an unchanged abstract. The full text describes a lightweight model trained on each dataset, with a frozen pretrained enzyme-bias component, and treats 'foundation' models as future work. The reusable artifacts are MIT code, CC-BY-4.0 reference bias models on Zenodo (transferable within an assay type) and per-dataset trained models on ENCODE/Synapse. No broad reusable pretraining is evidenced, and no written policy covers assay-specific predictors. Re-reviewed 2026-10-10; see evidence/refresh-2026-10-10/hold_reviews.json.
review.reconsider_when: Reconsider if a written scope policy explicitly admits assay-specific sequence-to-function predictors or model compendia of per-dataset checkpoints, or if the developers release and document a single pretrained ChromBPNet-family model intended for reuse across datasets or cell contexts.

record.name: Mistral-DNA
record.description: Family of small causal DNA language models by Raphaël Mourad that reduce the Mixtral-8x7B mixture-of-experts architecture for genomics. Public v1 checkpoints (1M-422M parameters) are pretrained on hg38 (10 kb sequences), with further checkpoints named for bacterial, yeast, Arabidopsis, viral and other corpora.
record.io: DNA sequence -> embeddings, next-token likelihoods (zero-shot variant scores), generated DNA; fine-tuned classification heads
record.status: HOLD: public ungated checkpoints with apache-2.0 model cards; repository code has no licence; no primary paper or technical report; README still links a non-public v0.1 checkpoint
record.use_cases: Genomic sequence classification, DNA generation, fine-tuning for regulatory/variant tasks, teaching/tutorials
record.audit_note: Re-reviewed 2026-10-10. Authorized checkpoint, direct model card and weight terms verified (v1 hg38 cards: apache-2.0, ungated, safetensors). The README-linked v0.1 checkpoint returns 401. Code repository has no licence. No primary paper or technical report was found (Europe PMC, arXiv, web search). GTN tutorials co-authored by the developer document reuse only.

review.reason: Re-reviewed 2026-10-10. Three of the four sub-conditions are now met: the developer's account has 15 public, ungated Mistral-DNA-v1 checkpoints with direct model cards, and the hg38 cards checked declare apache-2.0. Still missing: a primary paper, preprint or technical report describing the released v1 checkpoints. The GitHub code has no licence file, and the README still links a v0.1 checkpoint that returns HTTP 401. Developer co-authored Galaxy Training Network tutorials document reuse of v1-17M-hg38 but are not a model report. Re-reviewed 2026-10-10; see evidence/refresh-2026-10-10/hold_reviews.json.
